item.title: New adaptation of A Christmas Carol showing at The Light in Wisbech
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New adaptation of A Christmas Carol showing at The Light in Wisbech
A new film adaptation of the Charles Dickens classic, A Christmas Carol, is currently showing at The Light cinema in Wisbech. Titled Ebenezer, the 12A-rated production features Johnny Depp in the lead role of Scrooge. The cast also includes Rupert Grint as Bob Cratchit and Ian McKellen as the ghost of Jacob Marley.
The film follows the traditional narrative of the miserly Scrooge being visited by three spirits on Christmas Eve. While the story remains largely faithful to the original masterpiece, this version provides additional background on the development of the protagonist's character. Tickets are available now for those looking to catch the festive feature at the local cinema.

item.title: Seven million pound investment at King’s Lynn port
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Seven million pound investment at King’s Lynn port
A seven million pound investment has seen a new industrial facility open at the Port of King’s Lynn. Associated British Ports has transformed a previously unused site at the junction of Edward Benefer Way and Estuary Road into a storage and processing hub for the company Azelis.
The purpose-built site includes over 4,000 square metres of storage space and a heavy-duty concrete yard. The project, constructed by Britcon, aims to improve cargo handling and supply chain efficiency in the region. North West Norfolk MP James Wild has welcomed the development, describing the project as a significant vote of confidence in the local economy and the port's role in supporting West Norfolk trade.

item.title: New online tool ranks Norfolk postcodes by safety
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New online tool ranks Norfolk postcodes by safety
A new interactive tool has been launched to rank UK postcodes based on their safety in the event of a national attack. The "Doomsday" checker assigns properties a score out of 100 and a safety rating from A to G, based on proximity to military bases, power stations, and other infrastructure.
In Norfolk, North Norfolk was identified as the safest region, with Cromer receiving a top rating of 10A. Conversely, areas near RAF Marham and Norwich were flagged as higher risk due to their proximity to military and utility sites. The tool, which considers factors like weather and access to medical care, is available for public use at inspectorwalls.com/doomsday.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/new-doomsday-tool-reveals-safest-postcodes-in-norfolk-sh-9491566/

King’s Lynn prepares for Christmas lights switch-on this Sunday
King’s Lynn will host its annual Christmas lights switch-on this Sunday, November 22, in the Tuesday Market Place. The event begins at 2pm with an afternoon of live music and entertainment, featuring performances from local school choirs and singer Sarah Mai. Hosted by Jeremy Durrant, the celebrations will culminate with the official switch-on at 5pm, performed by the Mayor of West Norfolk, Councillor Steve Bearshaw.
Further festive activities are scheduled for the town throughout December, including a Christmas market and Santa-themed events. Meanwhile, residents in Downham and Hunstanton can look forward to their own local switch-on celebrations, which are set to take place the following weekend on Sunday, November 29.

New venue The Fat Badger to open in North Wootton
A new business, The Fat Badger, is set to open in North Wootton this December. Located on Ling Common Road at the site of the former House on the Green, the venue aims to serve as a social space rather than a traditional pub. Owners Neil Williamson and Mark Wilson have renovated the premises to offer coffee, brunch, and all-day breakfast, alongside fish and chips and pizzas sourced from their other local businesses.
The venue features a bar, dining areas, and a chilled upstairs space equipped for sporting events. The site also includes a courtyard with pétanque facilities and welcomes dogs. The team is also accepting bookings for private events, including christenings and wakes.

item.description:

Clenchwarton man sentenced for e-bike theft and drug-driving
A 32-year-old man from Clenchwarton has been sentenced after admitting to theft and drug-driving offences at Lynn Magistrates’ Court. Shane Wilson was found in possession of a stolen £700 e-bike in Norwich this July, which had been tracked by its owner.
In a separate incident on April 4, Wilson was stopped by police while riding a motorbike at 45mph in a 30mph zone. Subsequent tests revealed he was over the legal limit for both cocaine and cannabis. Wilson has been handed an 18-month community order, including 40 hours of unpaid work and a mental health requirement. He is also banned from driving for 32 months and must pay a £114 victim surcharge.

Businesses in King’s Lynn have voted to continue the Discover King’s Lynn initiative for another five years. The organisation, which was first established in 2017, aims to attract visitors and support the local economy through events and various campaigns.
BID chairperson Sharon Edwards thanked the team and local partners, including the borough council and Norfolk Police, for their ongoing cooperation. The group now plans to implement its next five-year business strategy to further develop the town centre as a place to work and visit.

Gaywood man’s football magazine shortlisted for national award
A West Ham United fanzine edited by a Gaywood resident has been shortlisted for a national honour. Blowing Bubbles, edited by TV journalist David Blackmore, is in the running for Fanzine of the Year at the 2026 Football Supporters’ Association Awards. This marks the fourth time the publication has reached the shortlist.
The winner will be announced at a ceremony in London on Monday, November 30. West Ham supporters have until midday on Monday, November 16, to cast their votes for the magazine. The publication, which launched in 2012, has now produced 173 editions, offering fans a platform to share their views on the club.
